rationale: Merge Vineyard Northeast into Vineyard Offshore because Vineyard Offshore is the manager-level CIP platform, while Vineyard Northeast is federal lease OCS-A 0522 and Vineyard Wind 2 is a project within that lease. Preserve the lease's 2019 joint-venture history and the 2022 CI IV acquisition as former/current ownership history on Vineyard Offshore, retain the procurement and permitting milestones, and retire the duplicate project-company row without merging distinct Vineyard Wind 1.

afterImage.name: Vineyard Offshore
afterImage.description: Vineyard Offshore is Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners' U.S. offshore-wind development platform, established in 2022 with federal lease interests held through CI IV. Its disclosed portfolio includes Excelsior Wind within OCS-A 0544 and Vineyard Northeast within OCS-A 0522, as well as other east- and west-coast developments. Vineyard Northeast is the lease and project identity for OCS-A 0522, whose current lessee is Vineyard Northeast LLC; Vineyard Wind 2 is a proposed project of up to 1.2 GW inside that lease, not a separate manager-level company. A 50/50 Avangrid and CIP joint venture won the lease in 2018 and it became effective on April 1, 2019. On January 10, 2022, a CI IV vehicle acquired Avangrid's interest and obtained 100% of the lease rights. Massachusetts provisionally selected 800 MW in September 2024, but Vineyard Offshore withdrew the bid on December 20, 2024 after Connecticut made no offshore-wind selection. The lease remains active, while FAST-41 permitting is paused to April 1, 2027; no PPA, FID, financing close, construction start, lease surrender, sale, CIP exit or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026. Vineyard Northeast, Vineyard Wind 2, Excelsior Wind and their lease SPVs are consolidated beneath this one platform record; Vineyard Wind 1 remains distinct.

milestones.event: Public platform materials state that Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners-supported Vineyard Offshore was established in 2022 with initial lease areas owned by Copenhagen Infrastructure IV.
Vineyard Offshore was established as CIP's U.S. offshore-wind development platform.
Vineyard Offshore announced New York's provisional selection of an earlier Excelsior Wind configuration, but the round closed without a final award or executed offtake.
Vineyard Offshore announced Vineyard Northeast as the OCS-A 0522 project identity for New England.
Federal lease OCS-A 0544 became effective for Vineyard Mid-Atlantic LLC, the lease SPV for the area containing Excelsior Wind.
BOEM issued its notice of intent to prepare an environmental impact statement for the broader Vineyard Mid-Atlantic project.
NYSERDA closed the 2024 offshore-wind solicitation without awards, leaving Excelsior's 1,350 MW bid uncontracted.
Federal lease OCS-A 0522 became effective to the 50/50 Avangrid and CIP Vineyard Wind joint venture.
A CI IV vehicle acquired Avangrid's OCS-A 0522 interest, giving CIP 100% of the lease rights and ending the prior joint venture.
Vineyard Offshore withdrew the provisionally selected 800 MW Vineyard Wind 2 bid after Connecticut made no offshore-wind selection; no PPA or ownership closing resulted.
The FAST-41 schedule was extended with Vineyard Northeast permitting paused to April 1, 2027 while the federal lease remained active.
